translated_text: Stricter industrial emission standards have made efficient and stable low-temperature denitration catalysts a priority for air pollution control. We will load manganese-cerium mixed oxide onto nanoscale titania to construct a core-shell catalyst for low-temperature selective catalytic reduction (SCR). We will combine in situ infrared spectroscopy with density functional theory calculations to clarify how manganese-cerium interfacial synergy regulates NH3 adsorption and activation. In preliminary work, our MnOx-CeO2/TiO2 catalyst converted more than 92% of NOx across the 150-250 °C window [1]. The analogous system reported in reference [2] (2020) deactivates readily in sulfur-containing atmospheres; we will therefore introduce yttrium doping to improve sulfur resistance. The expected outcomes will inform diesel vehicle exhaust purification and offer both mechanistic insight and application value.
